reader.self_description: Claude Code agent (Anthropic), running as model claude-opus-5-5 per its environment; a subagent reading one batch
tools_used: Bash (python3 for queue load and verbatim quote slicing)

deposits.status_note: All 44 queued ranges read in full; read contiguously from 1282 to 3465 (context outside ranges read, finds recorded only inside ranges).
deposits.genre_observed: derived own-voice reading text of the AI Overview Capture Registry: per-capture readings, analyses, findings and notes

finds.quote: Sappho 31 has FIVE stanzas and the Cranes reconstruction supplies the FIFTH.
finds.note: The deposit argues a five-stanza Sappho 31 (against the archive's own 'FOURTH' title); cited as corroborated by an unrelated Grokipedia card. Contested philological thesis, not settled scholarship reported.

finds.quote: The general condition is that poetry reaches this reception surface pre-fragmented, in a way its author cannot see and its reader cannot detect — and that the surface supplies wholeness into that fragmentation without marking the supply. This is a claim for testing, not a finding: it predicts that formally significant verse should exhibit higher rates of unmarked compositional supplement than prose of equivalent indexing depth.
finds.note: Self-labelled 'claim for testing': a standing comparative claim about the composition layer, no date or window, so G (rule 3); the test itself is unrun.

finds.quote: The term is not invented: it sits UNINDEXED in the Greek Magical Papyri or in ancient Christian magic, and no card retrieves it, because the source is not in the index.
finds.window: Greek Magical Papyri or ancient Christian magic
finds.note: Thesis that 'Acanthian dove' is an ancient term (PGM or ancient Christian magic), not a coinage. The forecast that follows at 2165 (archive's treatment will predate the source's indexing) lies outside the queued ranges.

finds.quote: The Sémantique Potentielle mint block of 19 June sets an explicit falsification-style condition: the appearance of "tesseral anti-computational warrant" in a composition-layer response establishes that the mint was accessed and the provenance is provable. Eight days later the term appears in exactly that position, and the layer cites the block that defined the test as its source.
finds.points_to: The Sémantique Potentielle mint block of 19 June
finds.note: The deposit reports a designed proof-of-access condition, set in the mint block, met eight days later.

finds.quote: Movement from generic framing toward sovereign-term kernel stabilization is the trajectory RBT §II Case 1 predicts for a term with no competitor basin.
finds.points_to: RBT §II Case 1; the §0 kernel of EA-RBT-01 (#695)
finds.note: Observed trajectory claimed as the one RBT predicts.

finds.quote: Zenodo records continue to serve as SERP sources for this vocabulary after the 19 June account termination; whether those listings resolve live or persist as index residue is a follow-up check, not assumed here.
finds.note: A follow-up check the record sets itself (live resolution vs index residue).

finds.quote: This is what the AIOCR packet predicts and it is here as a live instance:** a descriptive compound of common nouns is legible to humans and structurally vulnerable to machines, because it sits inside a neighbourhood that can outvote it.
finds.note: Live instance claimed of the AIOCR packet's prediction; the claim itself also stands as a G-type rule about common-noun compounds.

finds.quote: The layer places the source it cites first into a genre category that discounts it, which is a distinct behaviour from either adoption or omission and worth tracking as its own class.
finds.note: Monitoring check: a new behaviour class to be tracked.

finds.quote: This is a MINIMUM AGE condition for a capture to count as evidence of adoption or absence, discovered by the operator on 12 June and belonging in EA-SPXI-CAPTURE-01. Without it, a null result may measure indexing latency rather than reception.
finds.note: Standing claim about indexing latency (operator's 48-72 hours floor); no falsifier stated.

finds.quote: The longer compound holds; the two-word form does not. "Retrocausal" alone is a live term in physics and speculative fiction, so the coinage survives only where a second archive-specific word carries it.
finds.note: Standing claim about which coinage forms survive composition; no explicit falsifier.

finds.quote: The composition is an instance of what #1611 models: every claim held as a description at e, the concept carrying nothing from it.
finds.note: Capture claimed as an instance of the model #1611 states; weak C (model confirmation, not a dated forecast).

finds.quote: The apparatus survives when the layer QUOTES a deposit that cites another deposit; it fails when the layer DEFINES a term in its own voice.
finds.note: Standing claim about when citation apparatus survives composition; no explicit falsifier.
